A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProteinTTT research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original structure, fitness, and function prediction experiments, including CAMEO, ProteinGym, MaveDB, SAbDab, and BFVD results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds DPLM2 and ProGen2 evaluations, a BFVD confidence-gain distribution, and detailed failure-case analyses.

M1.justification: v2 only suggests extending customization to autoregressive models. v3 implements teacher-forced next-token customization for ProGen2 using a new objective in Appendix B. This extends the existing framework; DPLM2 uses the existing masked-modeling objective.

E1.justification: The evaluated datasets, protein populations, and structure, fitness, and function tasks remain the same. The new model evaluations use retained benchmarks, and Figure A13 examines existing CAMEO cases. Protein design and complex prediction remain proposed future applications.

E2.justification: v3 substantially broadens the evaluated model families beyond bidirectional masked models. Table 1 adds DPLM2 Bit-based with and without ProteinTTT; Tables 2 and A4 add ProGen2-small and ProGen2-large with corresponding uncustomized comparisons. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce DPLM2 settings including a 650M model, 100 denoising steps, and 10 customization steps, plus ProGen2 model sizes and customization budgets. Existing splits and metrics remain unchanged. Table 2 corrects the reported ProteinGym protein count from 217 to 186 while retaining 217 assays, without establishing resampling.

E4.justification: v3 adds a distribution of BFVD confidence improvements (Figure A12) and detailed analyses of two existing CAMEO failures, 7QII chain B and 7MQ4 chain A (Figure A13). Table A4 also extends MSA-depth analysis to ProGen2. Earlier hyperparameter, customization-step, and runtime analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies a paired t-test with p < 0.05 for the SAbDab comparison. Five-seed standard deviations and the existing bootstrap confidence-interval procedure are retained. Table 2 removes the previously stated upper bound on omitted phenotype-specific standard deviations.

E6.justification: Existing tabulated performance values are retained, but v3 adds results across two additional modeling paradigms. New base-versus-customized comparisons report DPLM2 TM-score 0.3701 versus 0.3796 and ProGen2-small/large average Spearman 0.3255 versus 0.3591 and 0.3724 versus 0.3817. Figure A12 additionally reports that 49.8%, 26.0%, and 5.8% of 317,882 BFVD proteins gain at least 5, 10, and 20 pLDDT points. These are newly reported comparisons, not performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix B introduces the formal autoregressive customization objective in Equation (4). The existing masked-modeling and MSA objectives, perplexity definition, and mathematical justification remain unchanged apart from renumbering; no new proof is provided.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and concluding discussion retain the same central claims: single-protein customization improves generalization across models and tasks, achieves state-of-the-art fitness prediction, and benefits antibody and viral structure prediction. The headline 19% BFVD claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 mainly offers general overfitting caveats and defers comprehensive failure analysis. New Appendix I substantially develops applicability boundaries, possible extensions, and the difficulty of controlling failures without reliable confidence metrics. Figure A13 specifically interprets two apparent degradations through missing dimer context and NMR conformational ambiguity.

D1.justification: Appendix F and Table A3 add checkpoint sources, denoising settings, precision choices, and hyperparameter grids for the new models. Existing hardware and package information remain unchanged. Some new details conflict: Appendix B states ProGen2 batch size one while Table A3 lists four, and the caption's ESMFold-only LoRA statement conflicts with the ProGen2-large row.

R1.justification: Appendix C newly acknowledges MSA evotuning precedents from Alley et al. (2019) and Gordon et al. (2024). Appendices B and I substantially expand research positioning around autoregressive and diffusion models, confidence estimation, and potential extensions to existing structure-prediction and protein-design systems.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v3 makes local rewrites, inserts appendices on additional model paradigms and limitations, repairs code-snippet references, and updates affiliations, acknowledgments, and the publication header.

P2.justification: Tables 1, 2, A3, and A4 gain model rows, and two supplementary figures are added. Existing appendix plots are relocated or renumbered; Figure 3 and the fitness example are reformatted, and the outdated ProteinPin labels are corrected. The overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens evidence for applicability beyond masked language models and adds concrete failure analysis, clearer limitations, and acknowledgment of MSA customization precedents. These improve the support and context of the retained conclusions. Conflicting new implementation details, particularly ProGen2's batch size and LoRA documentation, limit reproducibility and keep the overall improvement modest.
